title: 音乐游戏《白金档案》将于9月10日正式上线1.0版本，两款新DLC同步登场
text:
近日，音乐游戏《白金档案》（PLATiNA :: LAB）的开发团队HIGH-END GAMES通过官方直播公开了1.0正式版本的前瞻信息。本作将于9月10日正式结束抢先体验、迎来1.0版本发售。
v1.0版本中，官方宣布游戏将加入 官方中文 支持。此前因语言门槛而持观望态度的玩家们，届时将可以无障碍地体验剧情与角色互动内容了。
与此同时，游戏本体价格也将迎来永久性大幅下调——伴随转正，游戏国区售价调整至60元，并在正式发售后将提供限时两周的 85折优惠 及 BUNDLE组合包优惠 。折算下来，仅需51元即可入手一款包含120余首可玩曲目、十余位Q萌角色相伴的音乐游戏，入手相当划算。
商店页链接： https://store.steampowered.com/app/3430470/PLATiNA__LAB/
数据世界，不止”打谱”
《白金档案》是一款以经典下落式玩法为核心的节奏游戏，提供4轨、6轨与进阶PLUS谱面，无论是音游入门新手，还是追求高难度的硬核玩家，都能找到适合自己的节奏。
但《白金档案》远不止”打歌”这么简单 —— 十余位个性鲜明的DB萌娘会在你演奏时陪伴左右。达成连击时她们会为你喝彩，出现失误时她们会给你鼓励，打谱这件事，从此不再是孤独的指尖修行。
作为音游的核心，游戏的曲库也是丰富多样，涵盖多种品类：从原创曲、Vocaloid、Anisong，到金属、爵士和经典游戏音乐，120余首曲目横跨十余种风格。无论大家是术力口老饕、J-POP爱好者，还是重型音乐狂热粉丝，都能在这里找到属于自己的那份节奏。
每首曲目均配有专属背景动画（BGA），玩家甚至可以在”观看背景动画”模式下单独欣赏喜欢的BGA。可以说，《白金档案》是一场可以玩的Live盛典！
1.0版本更新，全方位体验升级
本次推出的1.0版本并非小修小补，而是在剧情、角色和游戏等多个维度进行的大规模更新。
在剧情方面，游戏第一章将在v1.0中正式上线，玩家将扮演拥有特殊天赋的解码者（Decoder），与研究员艾琳、斑比和小蛋糕一同探索被加密的数据世界，与此同时，档案室还迎来了6位拥有独立个性和背景故事的全新DB角色。
游戏还会新增“我的数据”功能，登录次数、持有道具数量、成长趋势等数据都能够得到系统化的呈现。
贴纸收集系统也将同步开启，完成游戏内重要目标即可获得Q萌贴纸，集齐后还可以补全收藏图鉴；全新实装的玩家排行榜，支持查看自己在指定谱面中的排名，并可浏览其他玩家的失误位置及判定详情。
而在自定义内容方面，游戏里新增了打击音效和称号两类选项，再加上原有的设备、音符、头像图标、个人资料背景等，玩家的个性化选择空间将得到进一步拓宽。
1.0版本中还将新增两个对新玩家来说颇为友好的功能，一是在游戏开始前增加了完整的教程关卡，帮助新玩家快速上手；二是曲库中绝大部分原本需要通过“研究日志”模式解锁的曲目，现均已默认常驻，新玩家购入后即可直接体验，无需额外解锁。
此外，所有DB角色还会新增好感度10级解锁的“留言”奖励，绝大部分角色新增7级解锁的“贴纸”奖励，EA期间已达到对应好感度等级的玩家在更新后可立即领取。
两款全新DLC曲包，随1.0同步登场
除了本体内容更新以外，两款全新DLC曲包，在版本更新之际将同步上线——
Table of Contents
DLC [SWEETIE;S]
迄今可玩曲目数量最多的DLC！收录24首全新原创歌曲。每首曲目均配有专属背景动画。更棒的是，DLC还将解锁DB角色小蛋糕（Cake）的全新皮肤，以及包含设备、音符等多种主题外观和头像装饰，在打谱的时候相伴在大家身旁。
DLC [Flagship Collection]
DLC [SWEETIE;S]
迄今可玩曲目数量最多的DLC！收录24首全新原创歌曲。每首曲目均配有专属背景动画。更棒的是，DLC还将解锁DB角色小蛋糕（Cake）的全新皮肤，以及包含设备、音符等多种主题外观和头像装饰，在打谱的时候相伴在大家身旁。
DLC [Flagship Collection]
这是为庆祝1.0正式发售推出的庆祝曲包，收录了来自韩国和海外风格各异的知名IP曲目，包括大热曲《恋爱循环》和《電波的妄想美少女Q》等等，其中部分曲目本体玩家还可免费游玩！两款付费原声带也同步推出，组合购买DLC或原声带可享受额外优惠。
所有在9月10日上午11:00（北京时间）永久降价前就已经购买并入库《白金档案》本体的玩家（包括通过Steam key激活的玩家，也需在此时间前完成激活入库），将在1.0发售时免费解锁以下专属回馈:
免费解锁DLC“SWEETIE;S” ——老玩家可直接入库上述收录24首原创曲目、定价82元的大型DLC。
2.3种限定纪念装饰道具！ 包括主题icon头像、动态纪念背景、EA玩家专属称号——这是专属于早期支持者的身份象征，永久纪念这份从EA阶段走到今天的旅程。
此外，为答谢各位玩家一直以来的支持与信任，游戏将于今年9月为所有玩家推送一次免费更新，追加全新Vocaloid原创曲目——《Earth Sci》。该曲此前在2026年The VOCALOID Collection（ボカコレ）夏季赛中斩获Rookie榜第9名的优异成绩。
现有系统，全面”翻新”
除了新内容的加入，游戏内已有的系统也迎来了新的优化：
选曲界面迎来了直观的升级。新版界面在分类筛选中加入了“新曲”与“热门曲目”等版块，并新增了排序与收藏功能，每首歌曲的通关状态展示也变得更加清晰——对于有“清谱”习惯的玩家来说，这份一目了然的进度，更能够增加继续游戏的动力。
细节上，DB角色的语音互动场景进一步拓展，在保持连击、完成段落、判定失误等多种情况下均可触发角色语音，让演奏过程更有陪伴感。
《白金档案》1.0版本将在9月10日于Steam正式发售。对这款游戏感兴趣的玩家，欢迎前往商店页了解更多信息。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3430470/PLATiNA__LAB

title: 《NBA 2K27》正式上线：这就是近年来最有诚意的一代 NBA 2K
text:
玩法全面焕新、五大传奇时代开启、百年传承篮球世家！全新《NBA 2K27》现已正式发售
2026年9月4日，2K正式宣布，由 Visual Concepts 开发的篮球模拟游戏《NBA 2K27》现已全球正式发售，登陆 PlayStation®5、Xbox Series X|S、PC（Steam）以及 Nintendo Switch™ 2 平台。
作为拥有超过二十年历史的篮球游戏系列，几乎每一年，玩家都会问同一个问题： 这一代《NBA 2K》，到底更新了什么？
而到了《NBA 2K27》，答案或许比过去几年都更加清晰。
从攻防系统重新调整到规模进一步扩大的辉煌生涯，从能够穿越多个篮球时代的全新玩法；再到篮球联盟、梦幻球队、自创球员系统乃至 Nintendo Switch 2 与 PC 版本的全面升级——《NBA 2K27》几乎对玩家熟悉的每一个核心模式都进行了不同程度的更新。
如果要用一句话概括《NBA 2K27》，那么它可能正是近年来最有诚意的一代 NBA 2K。
游戏玩法：从攻到防，篮球玩法重新调整
对于一款篮球游戏来说，最终决定体验的始终是球场上的48分钟。
《NBA 2K27》继续采用 ProPLAY® 技术，并针对进攻和防守两端进行了全面调整。
进攻端，玩家拥有了更多创造空间的方法。从穿越步、上下步，到进一步开放的自定义运球体系，持球进攻不再单纯依赖某几个强势动作，而是给予玩家更多根据防守选择进攻方式的空间。
防守端的变化同样明显，全新的举手防守、重新设计的投篮干扰系统、更丰富的防守拦截以及新的身体碰撞机制，让防守球员拥有更多能够真正影响进攻的手段。与此同时，焕新的“主宰”系统以及进一步提升的 AI，也让每个攻防回合拥有更多变化。
换句话说，《NBA 2K27》真正 让进攻和防守重新回到更加均衡、更加依赖技术的状态。
生涯模式：五大传奇时代任你选择，辉煌生涯迎来近年来最重磅升级
一直以来，“从无名球员成长为 NBA 超级巨星”都是辉煌生涯最核心的幻想。
而《NBA 2K27》把这个幻想进一步扩大了。
全新的生涯模式，让玩家能够进入五个不同的传奇篮球时代征战 NBA。
这意味着，你的职业生涯不再只能发生在当下。
你可以进入属于不同巨星、不同球队和不同篮球风格的历史时期，用自己的自创球员重新书写联盟历史。
与此同时，《NBA 2K27》还准备了系列迄今规模最宏大的电影化辉煌生涯故事—— 《Fire & Concrete》 ，讲述一段属于现代篮球世界的逆袭故事。
而对于喜欢和朋友一起玩的玩家来说，还有另一项系列首次加入的内容：
玩家终于可以与好友共同踏上属于自己的 NBA 生涯之路，从现实到游戏都成为球场好搭档！
篮球联盟：不只是在球场打球，也可以亲手创造一个横跨100年的篮球世界
喜欢经营球队的玩家，同样是这次《NBA 2K27》升级的重点对象。
篮球联盟模式重新强化了球队经营体验，包括玩家长期呼声较高的阵容管理工具、更完善的劳资协议与合同谈判系统，以及全新的  GM Trust  机制。
但更值得关注的，是全新的“百年传承”。
在这一玩法中，《NBA 2K27》将打造一个跨度达到 100年 的篮球宇宙，并加入球员锁定与 RPG 式成长体验。
你可以管理球队，也可以跟随一名球员经历联盟的变化。
一代球星退役，新人进入联盟；球队兴衰交替，纪录不断被重新书写——玩家亲手创造的篮球世界，将真正拥有属于自己的历史。
篮球之城：男女同场竞技，《NBA 2K27》的篮球之城迎来重要改变
如果说玩法调整解决的是“球怎么打”，那么这一代“篮球之城”的改变，则直接拓展了“谁能一起打球”。
在《NBA 2K27》中，玩家首次可以创建女性自创球员，并带入篮球之城。
更重要的是，男性与女性自创球员如今可以在篮球之城的多人模式中 真正实现同场竞技 。
所有自创球员均基于相同框架打造，以保证竞技环境中的公平性。这也是 NBA 2K 系列首次在篮球之城中实现男女球员共同参与多人比赛。
与此同时，篮球之城本身也迎来了大量更新。
篮球中心、剧院、竞赛球场以及 Seasonal Parks 均拥有全新场景；篮球中心比赛将在五个不同场地间轮换；“街头之王”迎来一座传奇球场；全新的“每日对决”则进一步强化每天的竞争与排名体验。
其中， 战队总部 成为队伍专属的大本营，玩家可以在这里进行训练、排位、私密比赛、战队成长以及赛季锦标赛；而全新的 休闲角 则为刚刚进入篮球之城的新玩家提供一个更加友好的起点。
从核心竞技玩家，到第一次踏入线上球场的新手，这一代篮球之城正在尝试容纳更多不同类型的玩家。
梦幻球队：“每一张卡都有价值”，梦幻球队重新思考卡牌养成
梦幻球队同样迎来了围绕玩家长期体验的一系列改变。
《NBA 2K27》提出了一个非常直接的设计理念：
每一张卡，都应该有价值。
为此，全新的“球员经验值”系统允许玩家通过实际游玩不断提升手中的球员卡，而扩展后的交易系统可以接受更多类型的球员卡。
拍卖行则首次实现 PS5、Xbox Series X|S 与 Nintendo Switch 2 平台统一，形成一个规模更大的社区卡牌市场。
此外，玩家熟悉的“在线三威胁”和“在线关键时刻”也将以轮换限时模式的形式回归。
梦幻球队不再只是不断寻找下一张更强的卡，也尝试让玩家已经拥有的阵容拥有更长的生命周期。
自建球员创建器：从捏人到养成，自创球员第一次拥有更多可能
对于大量 NBA 2K 玩家来说，每一代游戏真正开始的地方，不是选球队，而是“捏人”。
《NBA 2K27》带来了系列迄今更加丰富的自创球员创建器。
全新的徽章代币、重新设计的徽章成长体系以及“协同作用”系统，让 build 的打造拥有更大的策略空间。
而随着女性自创球员正式加入，玩家可以第一次创建属于自己的女性球员，并直接进入男女同场竞技的篮球之城。
这不仅仅是增加一个角色选项，也意味着从人物创建、成长路线到线上竞技，《NBA 2K27》的自创球员体系正在变得更加完整。
Switch 2 首次支持60帧，PC版进一步挑战画质上限
《NBA 2K27》的升级并不仅仅发生在游戏模式中。
Nintendo Switch 2 版本首次加入  60 FPS 性能模式 ，同时提供强调画面表现的画质模式。
针对 Switch 2 的硬件特性，本作还加入三分大赛、街头篮球玩法、扣篮大赛、Pop-a-Shot 等体感小游戏，并支持 GameShare 和完整鼠标操作。
PC 平台方面，《NBA 2K27》支持 NVIDIA DLSS 5。
通过针对 GeForce RTX 50 系列 GPU 引入 3D-Guided Neural Rendering（3D 引导神经渲染）技术，游戏将在材质、光照以及整体画面真实感方面获得进一步提升，同时保持球员扫描的还原度。
这一次，《NBA 2K27》想给每一种玩家一个回来的理由
每年推出一款体育游戏，最大的挑战从来不是加入多少新内容。
而是如何让老玩家重新感受到变化。
有人一年只玩辉煌生涯，有人每天泡在篮球之城；有人沉迷梦幻球队，也有人可以在篮球联盟里模拟几十个赛季；还有玩家只想约上朋友，随时打一场球。
因此，《NBA 2K27》这一代最值得注意的地方，也许并不是某一个孤立的新功能。
而是几乎每一类玩家，都能找到属于自己的变化。
从重新调整攻防平衡，到男女自创球员首次同场竞技；从五大传奇时代，到合作辉煌生涯；从100年的篮球联盟宇宙，到重新设计的梦幻球队养成；再到 Switch 2 的60帧体验与 PC 画质升级——这些变化最终指向了同一个目标：
让篮球世界拥有更多玩法，也让玩家拥有更多选择。
这或许也是为什么，《NBA 2K27》可以被称作近年来最有诚意的一代 NBA 2K。
现在，新的赛季已经开始。 Ball Over Everything！

title: 星途闪耀，共赴天城！神明养成蜕变卡牌手游《星途天城》预约开启！
text:
神明养成蜕变卡牌手游《星途天城》现已开启全平台预约！
游戏将蒸汽朋克、神秘学与神话幻想融入同一片异世界大陆，涵盖角色进阶养成、策略对战、浮空世界探索、玩家联机作战等丰富玩法，兼顾丰富游玩体验与策略深度，感兴趣的游戏爱好者们千万不要错过！
玩家将以来自异世界的原初之神身份，踏入浮空世界「埃努玛」，在众神混灭的时代重新引发神迹，协助星灵重塑神格、抵抗灾厄，守护天城，开启一场充满未知的星途冒险。
一、集结出发：召集星灵，组建专属队伍
在游戏设定中，玩家醒来后将成为天启特命局的特别调查员，同时也是被神格选中的“神明”。关于过去的记忆尚未完全恢复，星途使者「摩罗斯」将陪伴玩家前行，协助调查员逐步找回失落的答案。
而这场冒险的第一步，是召集星灵并组建属于自己的小队。在埃努玛，“群星”是最高的信仰，被群星选中的人会获得特殊能力，成为能够洞察灾厄、净除不洁的星灵。不同星灵拥有不同的能力、定位与性格，也将成为战斗中的核心战力。
二、降神养成：三阶觉醒，成长进度全员共享
玩家召集星灵后，需要根据敌人与玩法调整阵容：谁负责输出，谁负责承伤，谁能提供治疗，谁又能在关键时刻改变战局，都需要由玩家自行判断。星灵还可以通过考核迎来“降神”进阶，力量与形态都将进一步提升，解锁更强的作战可能。
在养成体验上，游戏提供了更轻量的成长方式。星灵等级与进阶进度可以共享，新获得的伙伴无需从头重复培养，玩家可以更快把新角色带上战场，让每一次召集都转化为阵容变化与策略尝试。
三、指尖策略：百变搭配，回合制战斗逆袭
《星途天城》打破传统卡牌的数值压制，创造丰富耐玩的回合制战斗体验。主角职业支持无损切换，技能百种组合搭配；玩家还可以结合星灵进阶与元素弱点等机制，根据不同战斗环境调整思路，持续尝试新的流派，在回合之间寻找逆袭机会。
当需要进一步强化阵容时，玩家可以前往“巴别之门”。该玩法需要两名玩家联机组队挑战强大Boss，合理分工与默契配合将成为通关关键。完成挑战后，玩家有机会获取适用于自身的装备，为后续灾厄调查提供强力战力支撑。
四、蒸汽幻想：复古美术，描绘浮空天城
游戏以蒸汽幻想为核心美术基调，将复古工业风，与神秘学、神话幻想的气质相融合，打造出兼具机械质感与奇幻色彩的浮空世界。七大地区拥有不同风格的城市景观，飞艇、星河与魔导建筑交织其中，构成一座充满想象力的复古蒸汽天城，让每一次探索都是新鲜冒险与复古美学的双重体验。
五、多元玩法：公会共战、世界 Boss 与轻松挂机
而在主线调查之外，游戏还提供了多种并行玩法。 玩家可以加入公会，与成员共享部分战果，组队挑战双人副本、讨伐世界 Boss，在配合与博弈中检验自己的阵容。游戏同时提供公平竞技、休闲玩法、社交与自由交易等内容，让调查任务之外，也能留出属于玩家自己的活动空间。
即使暂时离开游戏，挂机闯关也会自动推进，离线同样能够获得收益。等玩家再次回到埃努玛，积累的资源可以继续投入星灵培养，让每次上线都能接上新的进度。
通往埃努玛的冒险邀请函正式发出，《星途天城》预约通道现已全面开放！快来见证星灵降神觉醒的战力蜕变，在蒸汽浮空世界里玩转策略对战！即刻前往预约，接下天启特命局的专属委托，和你的星灵小队一起开启这场奇妙旅途吧！

title: Voting extended for special categories in the Best Places To Work Awards
text:
Now that Gamescom is firmly behind us, the GamesIndustry.biz team is busy judging the entries for this year's Best Places To Work Awards. Entries have closed for our headline awards, which are judged based on anonymous employee feedback - but we have extended the deadline for nominations for our Special Awards, which reward excellence in specific fields.
Nominations for the below categories will be accepted until midnight on Monday 7th September. These awards are separate from the main BPTW categories, and are open to all UK businesses working in and with the games industry.
The Diversity Award
The Green Award
HR Hero Award
Training and Development Award
Education Award
Corporate Social Responsibility Award
Health and Well-Being Award
Nominations can be made by internal or external parties, and judging will be completed next week ahead of the awards ceremony on October 1st.
Tickets are still available for the GamesIndustry.biz HR Summit , which this year is focused on the future of People & Work, and takes place during the day ahead of the Awards.

title: Xbox adds monthly cloud limits to Game Pass as it "continues to invest in its reliability and performance"
text:
Xbox will introduce monthly cloud gaming limits for Game Pass subscribers beginning in November 2026.
As laid out in a blog post , Game Pass Essential will be limited to five hours, Premium to ten hours, and Ultimate to fifteen hours per month.
After reaching these limits, subscribers may purchase additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store. Xbox noted that "available hours, purchasing options, and cloud gaming features may vary by market."
Xbox anticipates that these limits will affect 4% of Game Pass subscribers and will provide additional pricing details at a later date.
The platform holder said it made the decision because "the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer."
"Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost."
Xbox also announced that from November, players can access Xbox cloud gaming without a Game Pass subscription by purchasing cloud playtime hours and streaming eligible owned games on supported devices.
It stated this "will provide another option for people who want occasional access to cloud gaming or do not want a recurring Game Pass subscription."
Xbox One owners will be able to play eligible Xbox Series X|S games "without requiring an immediate hardware upgrade."
In July, Xbox began testing ad-supported game streaming , with ads shown before each session while core gameplay remains unchanged.
Xbox said the test is "designed to help give people more affordable ways to play on devices they already own."
"When done well, advertising can help lower the cost of access. It creates another way for players to get into games without an upfront streaming purchase and expands audiences through new ways to play."
These initiatives are part of CEO Asha Sharma's plan to focus on "efficiency and affordability alongside performance."
"With the crisis that's currently happening in hardware and components, it is absolutely something all of us need to be thinking about and innovating on and giving people more choice in terms of how they play their console and how they purchase their console."

title: GTA 6 Netflix preview causes PlayStation and Xbox hardware sales to jump in the UK
text:
PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S console sales increased in the UK following last week's Grand Theft Auto 6 reveal on Netflix .
According to The Games Business , Nielsen IQ data shows PS5 sales rose by 33% and Xbox console sales grew by 34%.
PS5 Pro consoles are selling out nationwide , and retailers including Argos and Smyths Toys now only have base models available.
Despite a significant jump in the run-up to GTA 6's launch in November, alongside Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 in October, Newzoo's Ronan Patrick said that it expects to see "an uptick in the install base but nothing particularly massive."
"The PS5 in inflation-adjusted terms is 67% more expensive [than at launch], and Xbox is twice as expensive," said Patrick.
"It's important to remember that the lion's share of time is often spent on older titles, and the closest analogy we have to a hardware shock is during the 2020-2021 GPU shortage, and you didn't see engagement or revenue being taken off course. You basically saw a reallocation of spend into software."
VGC reports that UK hardware sales are down 14.4% year-on-year, primarily due to a 32% decline in PS5 sales. Xbox Series X|S sales have increased by 3.1%.
The extended GTA 6 preview was Netflix's most-viewed title last week , reaching 31.1 million views in four days. On YouTube , the preview received 22 million views in one week.
Sensor Tower data shows that Netflix's US mobile viewership increased by 35% hour-over-hour during the premiere.

title: Future imperfect: Five predictions for the next decade | Opinion
text:
A lot of minds around the industry currently seem focused on one thing: the future. Whether it was Amir Satvat's Gamescom Dev keynote , or the plethora of industry luminaries who lined up to discuss ongoing and impending turmoil for Edge magazine's latest issue, the topic of the moment is what's next – and the mood is apprehensive, to say the least.
While not everyone is catastrophising, nobody seems to be outright rejecting the framing of "Crash 2.0" either. The spectre of the 1983 videogame crash looms large, though we can't read too much into its invocation in this particular moment. The industry does have an occasional flair for the dramatic and a habit of raising the spectre of desert pits full of E.T. cartridges at the first sign of market turbulence, after all.
Before talking about the future, in fact, let's talk briefly about the past. 1983 wasn't a downturn or a rebalancing; it was a near-collapse of industry revenues from over $3 billion in 1983 to a mere $100 million by 1985. Analysts justifiably wondered out loud whether video games themselves had been a passing fad that would now fade into obscurity.
We're not at the stage of burying games in the desert | Image credit: taylorhatmaker - Atari E.T. Dig: Alamogordo, New Mexico, CC BY 2.0
We are not facing anything like that. This is cold comfort to anyone who has seen their job or company disappear, or watched their labour of love sink beneath the waves of discoverability on launch, but the industry's headline revenue numbers are fine. Even if Sony was still going to let us have physical copies of anything, we wouldn't be burying them in the desert. Games are a firmly established medium with a huge audience; at this point, wondering if there's any future for video games is no more sensible than asking if people will soon get over this whole listening-to-music fad.
So if not a catastrophic crash, what exactly are we facing? Why is everyone so convinced that the industry's fortunes are perched on a knife-edge right now?
"The woes of 2026 look more like an intersecting set of factors that are all coming to a head at once"
Unsurprisingly, given the size, complexity, and reach of the modern games business, there's no one neat answer to that question. The roots of 1983's crash make for a satisfactory elevator pitch: an immature market with narrow appeal was flooded with low-quality products and tipped over the edge by a price war in the neighbouring home computer market. By comparison, the woes of 2026 look more like an intersecting set of factors that are all coming to a head at once.
Some of those factors are obvious and often discussed. The wild rise in the price of hardware components that are crucial to every gaming device shows no sign of easing off in the near term , forcing console price hikes and making PC upgrades almost prohibitively expensive. Development costs for games have skyrocketed, with budgets of over $100 million now routine, and $300–400 million budgets being relatively common at the high end of AAA. And then there's the concentration: more and more of the revenue and attention on every platform is being monopolised by a smaller and smaller set of gigantic games, the business models of which are often increasingly focused on extracting more revenue from existing players.
Marvel's Spider-Man 2 allegedly had a budget of around $300 million, according to documents leaked in 2023 | Image credit: Insomniac Games
But there are other factors at play here, too. It's no coincidence that the industry started to convulse with massive layoffs right around the time when interest rates – which had largely held close to zero since the 2008 financial crisis – shot upwards in 2022. Financing dried up across the board as investors reconsidered the risk profile of video game projects, and companies reeled in expensive speculative ventures they'd launched when money was practically free. The boom around generative AI delivered the coup de grace, sucking up any potential tech investment money for miles around, which was instead thrown at the very data centres that are making gaming hardware unaffordable.
Meanwhile, China has become a major force in game development and publishing; it's often still overlooked in the West, but you could argue that Sony's failed attempt to pivot to live service games was less about wanting the next Fortnite and more about wanting the next Genshin Impact. And alongside it all, there's the foundational malaise that's troubled the entire tech industry for the past decade – the failure of every attempt to introduce a new technology with the same transformational potential as smartphones in the late 2000s, or the internet a decade or so before that. Concepts like VR, AR, or the metaverse have largely failed to make a dent on the mass market.
Genshin Impact, developed by the Chinese studio MiHoYo, became a global hit after its release in 2020 | Image credit: MiHoYo/HoYoverse
Some of those factors are interrelated; some of them are internal to the industry and some are entirely out of its control. Nobody knows for sure how any one of them will play out in the end, let alone how the complex interactions between them will shape the coming years. "People will figure out how to make computers understand and output natural language, and it will make PlayStations really expensive" wasn't on anyone's bingo card for this decade.
Even within that tangled mess of probabilities, though, there are a few strands that look reasonably certain. Let's do a little light prognostication, and hope it all turns out more Hari Seldon than Madame Web .
Budget growth is slowing – but won't stop
Playable Worlds CEO (and MMORPG legend) Raph Koster cited some figures in the Edge article suggesting that inflation-adjusted budgets for games have risen from around $1 million in the mid-nineties to $10 million by 2005, and eventually to $100 million by 2015. By that growth rate, we'd expect to routinely see billion-dollar budgets at this point, but GTA 6's budget allegedly breaking through that ceiling is instead considered an eye-popping outlier. Budget inflation has slowed somewhat, largely because it's running into some mechanical limits – few companies can finance budgets at this scale, and even among those that can, the risk profile is unappealing. The idea that you could release a game that makes hundreds of millions of dollars and still lose money is enough to start putting a ceiling in place over all but the biggest, surest bets.
No official figures have been given for GTA 6's budget, but it is speculated to be one of the most expensive games ever made | Image credit: Rockstar Games
We have to acknowledge that there are market forces pushing in the opposite direction too, though. Few, if any, other games will ever justify a budget on the scale of GTA 6, but that game will establish player expectations nevertheless; on some level, every other game (but especially those in an adjacent genre or setting) will be compared to it for years to come. The arms races for graphical fidelity, environmental detail, or open world size don't disappear just because the budget numbers start getting unpalatable, and will continue to drive inflation at the very top end.
"Teams that can deliver polished-looking titles at budgets in the tens rather than hundreds of millions will be greatly in demand"
The slow-down of the hardware upgrade cycle that will be forced by the component pricing crisis will offer some breathing room here – lots of companies are going to put off tooling up for the next generation for several years past their original plans. Figuring out creative ways to do more with less (in terms of both finance and hardware) is already a hugely valuable skill in the industry, and this will only become more prominent; teams that can deliver polished-looking titles at budgets in the tens rather than hundreds of millions will be greatly in demand. Short-cuts will prove disappointing in the end; generative AI tools will likely become a fixture of very specific, ringfenced parts of development (notably on the programming side), but will do little to reduce team sizes or cut budgets, and in the short term might actually have the opposite effect.
AI will make its mark, but perhaps not where you expect
It's almost a certainty at this stage that the AI investment bubble – vastly over-inflated and driven on increasingly wild financial projections and impossible science fiction promises – is going to either pop or (hopefully) deflate in the coming months or years. Once we're through that turmoil, though, the foundational technology of generative AI will continue to exist, and much of it will be usable on consumer-grade hardware (which you'll even be able to buy at an affordable price again once the bubble is over). Once the desperate hope of a trillion-dollar IPO no longer rests on convincing the world that AI can do anything and everything, the more realistic set of things it can actually do will come into focus.
Roblox has already added some agentic AI creation tools | Image credit: Roblox
For the games business, AI's biggest impact won't be in development (where its uses will be quite limited), but in user generated content (UGC). The great barrier to UGC at present is that more powerful tools that can create more varied and interesting content tend to become exponentially harder to use, with a learning curve that's more and more offputting for ordinary users. AI tools that can interpret a user's natural language prompts to coordinate those tools and build levels, minigames, and other content are a natural and reasonably low-cost application for LLMs, and will spur a major boom in UGC-driven titles as adoption becomes more widespread.
"AI tools will spur a major boom in UGC-driven titles"
Existing titles like Roblox will have a platform advantage, but we'll see a glut of new UGC games emerging to try to carve out a slice of this market. The real difficulty will lie in solving discoverability and ecosystem issues; LLM-driven creation will democratise content creation on these platforms, but at the cost of making it increasingly difficult for any user's content to rise above the crowd. The real break-out titles of this kind will be those that take a different approach to UGC, stepping away from the "be your own game developer" concept and instead leaning into allowing players to create content aimed at customisation and personalisation of in-game appearances, experiences, and interactions.
The industry's centre of gravity will shift
The past few years of mass layoffs in western countries (especially North America) and extensive hiring in China have already shifted the industry's centre of gravity towards Asia to some degree, but the broader effects have been limited by the relatively closed nature of China's own market. The global importance of Chinese games (and Chinese investments) has grown, but the importance of the Chinese market itself – despite its scale – remains muted.
Emerging markets like Latin America will spur industry growth – Gamescom Latam in São Paulo (pictured here) is already growing from year to year, with attendance up 17.5% in 2026 | Image credit: Abragames
Short of a major policy reform in China, that won't change much in the coming years, but companies from all around the world, China included, will find themselves in heated competition for stakes in major emerging markets. As audience sizes in mature markets stagnate, developing markets in Southeast Asia, Latin America, and elsewhere, which are tipping over into having a sizeable middle class, will be the industry's best source of growth. Local tastes and engagement patterns will require significant adaptation, however, and western companies won't have a special head start; for young people in those regions, games from Chinese companies like MiHoYo and NetEase are as relevant and hold as much cachet as western or Japanese IPs.
"Developing markets will be the industry's best source of growth"
Don't overestimate the market's geographical shift, though. Whatever geopolitical and economic strife we may see in the coming years (let's conservatively predict "a lot"), the sheer market sizes of North America and Europe will remain dominant for the foreseeable future. The cachet of the United States as the world's cultural centre also won't be toppled easily. Companies will want to retain a foothold in the US, even if the cost of developing games there means the actual work is increasingly being done overseas. Consequently, we will end up in a situation where many of the industry's most high-profile creators are US-based, but few full-scale AAA development studios exist there any more.
Concentration will get worse…
In his Gamescom Dev keynote , Amir Satvat noted that 50–60% of the industry's revenue is going to just the top 20 games. I'd love to say that will become more fragmented and equitable, but it's hard to think of a scenario where that actually happens.
A few years ago, former Xbox head Phil Spencer lamented that losing the PS4/Xbox One generation was a near-unrecoverable blow , because that was the generation where people built up large digital game libraries – creating a massively powerful platform lock-in effect when they were choosing their next console. That's increasingly the case not just for platforms, but for individual games.
Gacha-style games, like Honkai Star Rail, are hard to leave behind | Image credit: HoYoverse
Gacha games are a straightforward example of this. How much of the repeat playing of gacha-style games is down to the fact that players have already invested a lot of time and money on their in-game accounts? Moving from a gacha game, where you've expended considerable resources on getting high-level characters and desirable customisations, to one where you're starting from zero creates an incredible level of friction that ordinary games have never had to overcome.
Now consider the boom in UGC I expect to arise from LLMs being integrated into creative tools, and ask yourself how hard it would be for a user to step away from a game which is filled not only with things that they bought, but things that they made (or at least, feel like they made). These kinds of mechanisms will concentrate attention and revenue in a shrinking pool of games that have locked players deep in their ecosystems.
…but indie breakouts will get bigger
At the other end of the scale and budgetary spectrum, however, the potential for independently developed games to skyrocket to massive success will also grow. Indie-style titles (the definition has become a bit blurred in recent years) already occupy most of the various tiers that used to exist under AAA , and big, breakout hits that recoup massive multiples of their budgets will be very prominent on the landscape.
Meccha Chameleon was a huge breakout hit this year, selling well over 15 million units | Image credit: lemorion_1224
That will create some false hopes – discoverability will be as tough as ever, and the median indie success will still look more like a well-executed genre title that pulls in predictable revenues from its niche market, rather than a runaway hit. Any kind of hopes, however, will help to attract investment to the sector, and big commercial successes will spur the logic of grassroots venture capital; in other words, invest relatively small amounts in lots of things on the hope that one of them will be the unicorn hit, earning mountains of money that more than make up for your losses elsewhere.
"Major indie breakthroughs will increasingly set the patterns that will be followed by massive AAA titles"
Those indie hits will also start being the prevailing winds of the industry's creative direction. We already see this to some extent, but major indie breakthroughs will increasingly set the patterns that will be followed by massive AAA titles a few years down the line. Hollywood has followed this playbook for years (expect lots of movies in years to come taking cues from Obsession or Backrooms), and games will follow suit, treating the indie scene as a creative incubator where risk is not only possible, but encouraged.
Five predictions. Drop a note in your calendar to check back in in five years' time and see how I did. If I've really missed the mark, I solemnly promise to watch all of Madame Web again in penance.

title: Nvidia acquires open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9bn
text:
Nvidia has acquired the artificial intelligence platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion.
As BBC News reports, Nvidia will pay about $11.9 billion to Hugging Face investors and may offer up to $1 billion in stock-based incentives. Amazon, AMD, and Intel are also investors in the open-source AI platform.
Nvidia president and CEO Jensen Huang wrote in a blog post that Hugging Face will stay open-source, and developers will not have to use Nvidia technology.
Huang said the deal will help Nvidia grow and improve Hugging Face's infrastructure for developers and organisations globally.
"Nvidia's infrastructure, engineering and global reach can help improve platform reliability, safety, model evaluation, inference and deployment capabilities, while preserving the open ecosystem that made Hugging Face foundational."
Hugging Face was founded in 2016 in New York City by French entrepreneurs Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond, and Thomas Wolf.
Delangue told CNBC that Hugging Face approached Nvidia because it "needed more resources, more scale, [and] more visibility." He described Nvidia as "a perfect home" for the platform.
Nvidia is the biggest contributor to Hugging Face, having released over 500 models and more than 250 open datasets.
"I am honoured that [Clément Delangue] came to me as he considered the next chapter of Hugging Face and believed Nvidia would be a great home for the company, its community and the future of open models," said Huang.
"We share this vision, and the Hugging Face team will now bring their passion and expertise to a much larger canvas, with their same iconic brand."
"To the millions of builders on Hugging Face: thank you for pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We can't wait to build the future together with you. Together, we will make AI more open, more capable and more accessible to people and institutions around the world."

title: Inside Tencent's long-term strategy: live service, AI tools, and evergreen titles
text:
Many column inches have been spent questioning the wisdom of focusing on live-service. Sony gambled and lost , as did many other companies chasing the dream of steady recurring revenues, while firms like Capcom that stuck to the traditional path have emerged relatively unscathed .
Highguard was one of the more recent live-service casualties , a game that was reportedly backed by the Tencent subsidiary TiMi Studio Group . But Tencent itself is not shying away from the glittering promise that live service titles bring.
Yong-yi Zhu
"I think our holy grail is live service, right?" says Yong-yi Zhu, VP and head of operations, strategy and compliance at Tencent Games.
"You look at Tencent's DNA, it's Honor of Kings, League of Legends, Valorant. They're games that build upon themselves, and it provides stability to the studio, it builds communities. And I think more and more games are about not just engaging people for a short period of time, it becomes a lifestyle."
The firm's sprawling, constantly shifting portfolio aspires to support that lifestyle. But a wide-ranging conversation with Zhu confirms that live service is only one part of its strategy.
Evergreen dreams
A lot has changed since GamesIndustry.biz last spoke with Zhu just under a year ago . The UK studios Splash Damage and Bulkhead have gone independent, following similar moves from The Chinese Room and Secret Mode earlier in 2025. Zhu won't go into details on the separation, but says "for certain studios we feel like we can't help them amplify their game."
Still Wakes the Deep maker The Chinese Room went independent from the Tencent-owned Sumo Group in 2025 | Image credit: The Chinese Room/Secret Mode
"What's really big for us is: does the partnership make sense? Are we bringing something to the table as much as the developers are bringing something to the table? And I think in those cases, either there was potentially a lack of synergy" – in terms of the games aligning with the firm's long-term strategy – "or there were just better opportunities." Ultimately, the firm decided they were "better standalone than they are with Tencent."
"There are certain situations where we acquire a studio and actually we have trouble integrating them"
Zhu is sanguine about not all of the company's many acquisitions working out. "There are certain situations where we acquire a studio and actually we have trouble integrating them because of market conditions or cultural differences," he says. "Not everything, at the end of the day, is going to be a slam dunk."
So what is the company strategy? Zhu says that evergreen titles are a key part of it – both single and multiplayer, with the former well-represented in the firm's mobile games portfolio – but ultimately "it's really about building sustainable communities long-term, having games that continue to engage with people." And while live service is the holy grail, it's not a singular focus. "It can be an IP that you build up," says Zhu. "This is not our game, but you look at Call of Duty: we consider that an evergreen IP, even though it's really one version after another."
Tencent owns Riot Games, maker of the perennially popular Valorant | Image credit: Riot Games
The ultimate aim is consistency: "You look at a lot of premium games: I think in the past, you've seen a lot of ups and downs with companies that launch a game and have to lay people off. I think more and more we're trying to bring stability, and you typically don't see Tencent doing the same thing."
The other key part of Tencent's strategy is investing in "really high quality talent," says Zhu, again emphasising that "it has to be synergistic between Tencent and the developer."
Doubling down
Zhu runs ops and strategy for Tencent's global games business, and has around 20 studios in his division. That includes Miniclip, Sumo Digital, Funcom, Fat Shark, Sharkmob, 10 Chambers, and Stunlock Studios in Europe, as well as Digital Extremes in North America and Grinding Gear Games in New Zealand.
The New Zealand-based studio Grinding Gear Games is behind Path of Exile | Image credit: Grinding Gear Games
His focus is "less about places we're about to go, and more about how we ensure these studios are successful in the launches that they're about to have." That includes making sure each receives appropriate support from the wider Tencent ecosystem on things like regional publishing, technical support, testing, backend services, or analysis: "Things like that where we provide expertise, because we've done it as Tencent in the domestic market, and now we're trying to translate that into the global market," says Zhu.
Related
Games for Change report aims to ground parental gaming concerns in "evidence rather than fear"
Raising Good Gamers white paper offers roadmap to better support families playing video games
He gives the example of experts from across China and Europe coming to help out on Dune Awakening. "They'll just sit alongside the devs at Funcom and work with them to solve the issues. And then afterwards, if it's an ongoing issue, sometimes they'll stick around. And sometimes we even say, 'Look, if it works out, the person can go to the studio and be a permanent employee'."
Funcom released Dune Awakening on PC in 2025, and it will launch on consoles on September 22 | Image credit: Funcom
He clarifies that things like creative and artistic design are mostly left to individual studios, but Tencent might swoop in to help on issues that are common across studios, like particular issues with Unreal Engine, or help with publishing in certain regions like MENA or Southeast Asia.
A question of scale
Funcom saw a wave of redundancies last October, and the Funcom-owned studio The Outsiders, maker of Metal: Hellsinger, was closed . At the time, Funcom said that the aim was to "focus our internal resources on releasing new content, features, and enhancements" for Dune Awakening. So is Tencent's strategy to focus more on bigger, live-service titles rather than smaller projects?
Related
Tencent, Xbox, Game Angels, Ansible and Flick to speak on Game Republic New Horizons investor stage
Games London also hosting a number of sessions and bringing a cohort of international investors to the show
"It really depends on the studio to be honest," says Zhu. He notes that Funcom had already been running the live-service title Conan Exiles for a long time when Tencent bought the studio. "So that's a part of their DNA. They design games to be live services, and we support them on that journey."
Conan Exiles was first released in 2018; Tencent bought Funcom in 2020 | Image credit: Funcom
Other studios in Tencent's portfolio, meanwhile, have tried live service, but it "didn't work out," and they have "now focused more on premium titles, because that's been their bread and butter. And for us, we really want to help build studios that are best in class in their craft, whatever that might be."
But how small is too small? Joe Brammer, CEO of Wardogs maker Bulkhead, told GamesIndustry.biz earlier this year that Tencent "wouldn't look at any game that was less than £50 million."
"I don't think there's anything that's stopping us from making smaller games"
Zhu disagrees. "I think we look at games across all scales, to be honest. I think for us, it's more about where the studio is on its journey and what its end destination might be. Could we help them get bigger? Sometimes we feel like, hey, our expertise doesn't quite match, or maybe the cultures don't match, but I don't think there's anything that's stopping us from making smaller games. We do have small games in our portfolio."
He describes Larian Studios and From Software are "north stars" in terms of Tencent's studio investments (the company owns a minority stake in both), and that they have "built up games over time, and not all of those games have been very big, but all of those games have been purposeful and have continued to build on the audience, and have continued to help them build on their craft. I don't think it's necessarily true that we don't look at smaller games."
Exdev
Last time we spoke , Zhu talked about spinning up some Chinese support teams, with the idea of tying Tencent's Western and Chinese arms together more closely. A year later, he says not as much progress has been made on this front as he would have liked, in part because of challenges working across different time zones. Instead, the focus has switched to trying to instill learnings from different studios across the group.
Star Wars: Galactic Racer, which is being published by the formally Tencent-owned Secret Mode, relied heavily on external development | Image credit: Fuse Games/Secret Mode
But he does see a future in the model of smaller, core teams being supplemented by external development: a model that has worked well for Star Wars: Galactic Racer . "At a high level, I think that makes sense," he says. "We were looking the other day at the development life cycle of Expedition 33, and it's a very similar story."
"For us, it's kind of how many people should we keep on staff and how many people should we then leverage from an outsource vendor? Sometimes it's like, 'Hey, we need high precision folks that are making very intricate things, and we would like them to all be in a certain location working together.' And that's kind of the prerogative of the studio head."
Location has proved a key factor in outsourcing, with some teams happy with distant partners, while others look for help in the same timezone. "And so we're looking across the globe at what the options are for our different studios. Sumo is potentially going to support our studios in Europe, because they're closer. But being in the UK, it's probably not the cheapest place to be. So you have trade-offs on these types of things."
"North America's a tougher and tougher place to be, unless you have a very solid dev team that has worked together for a long time"
This brings to mind Amir Satvat's fascinating keynote speech at Gamescom Dev , which pointed out that jobs are disappearing in expensive locales like California, but opening up in regions like Asia. As Satvat put it: "Head count moving from basically North America to basically anywhere else."
Zhu agrees that in general, "North America's a tougher and tougher place to be, unless you have a very solid dev team that has worked together for a long time. I came previously from Activision, where we were roughly all in the Santa Monica area, but it's a team that's delivered content year over year over year over year." For support teams, though, "it doesn't make sense to be in such an expensive part of the world."
The shift to AI
It was notable that this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live featured a large number of highly polished games from Chinese studios – which leads us to wonder whether we're seeing a power shift in the games industry from West to East.
"I would say I hope so," laughs Zhu. "I was born in China. But I think the reality is games like [Black Myth] Wukong really inspired people to make really high quality content. They now know what really, really good looks like for console and PC."
"I think a lot of Chinese developers are like, 'I know how to make high quality mobile games', and now they're like, 'Oh, this is what good looks like for console and PC'. I think probably in the past they've done a lot of art outsourcing and things like that that were a little bit lower level, but now they're like, 'We know what it looks like.' And then probably they have better tooling that can help them on things. And so it cuts that barrier and that gap."
"China in general really loves AI as a tool"
That better tooling includes "things like AI that can help people iterate more," says Zhu. "And AI for us is not about replacing people. It's about making people more effective and efficient across a number of different things. We have development teams that are a bit smaller, but they're like, hey, now we can make more content, we didn't want to be a big development team. We like our family feel of 30, 40 people, but now we're able to make higher quality things, and iterate more, and come up with cooler looking – whatever it is that they're designing."
"I think that's probably true of the Chinese developers, too, because they're kind of growing up in this age of leveraging tools," he says. "China in general really loves AI as a tool."
In the West, by contrast, developers tend to be more reluctant to use AI, with ethical concerns, copyright worries, and player backlash all front of mind. "I think people should just not be afraid of AI," says Zhu. "It's like the internet, it's coming. And I spent some time personally to figure out what is the best way to leverage AI in my daily life to make myself more efficient."
"I think people should just not be afraid of AI. It's like the internet, it's coming"
He thinks that development teams should be more "open to that way of thinking" and should consider AI as "a genuine tool."
"And there's honestly so many tools now, whether it's in coding, whether it's in art, whether it's in whatever else you've got: it can do so much for you."
He says that Tencent generally encourages developers to use AI, "because we think there's a lot of potential, but again, as a tool. I think on content generation, that's a very different conversation. I think that's probably further away. For development, it's more like we use this for concept art, we figure out what it's like, then we'll use AI tools for rigging, for motion matching, for code review. There's so many different things in the pipeline that [AI] can do. Even production management tools, they'll have AI bots in their Slack channel asking people for homework and things like that. So it can be used in a number of different ways that's not replacing humans, right?"
He acknowledges that there are still some difficulties to work through, not least when it comes to the copyright status of content produced via generative AI. "I do think that's something that the AI industry will have to figure out," he says. "Let's say the AI is only using our own libraries, right? That makes it very easy, because that's our IP, we've done it in the past, and they've remixed that content into something else. I think that's OK versus using something that's from a different content creator or just the general web. And we look at that very closely. We make sure that our data is confined to our studios."
This includes agreements with each tool provider to ensure that data doesn't end up being accessible outside the building. "What we don't want is our developers creating things that then get picked up from somewhere else, and then suddenly you've got versions of our things in a different game."
The formerly Tencent-owned Bulkhead recently released Wardogs in Early Access | Image credit: Bulkhead/Team17
With the backing of its vast parent, Tencent Games is in a position to experiment, placing bets large and small on a wide variety of products and studios. While it's recently retreated from Bulkhead and Splash Damage, and redirected AAA studio Lightspeed , our conversation took place the day after it announced a minority investment in W4 , the commercial development partner of the Godot engine. It seems likely that come next Gamescom, Zhu will have some different projects to talk about. But the throughline is engagement, whether via live service or not.
"At the end of the day, I sit in games, which is a part of a bigger Tencent ecosystem, and my purview is always about how do we keep people engaged, make sure that they're having fun," he says. "Because, to say in a crass way, that translates to the bottom line. The more people love your game, the more they're going to play your game."

title: Supercell's acquisition of Metacore expected to close this month
text:
Once the deal is closed, Merge Mansion will officially become part of Supercell's live games portfolio.
Supercell, the company known for the likes of Clash Royale and Brawl Stars , has signed a deal to acquire Merge Mansion developer Metacore.
The acquisition, which is expected to be completed at the end of September, is the latest example of major restructurings in the mobile game space. This deal itself comes as t Metacore, which restructured in May ahead the decision behind its own restructuring was to "better align with the core business, improve efficiency of operations, and respond to an increasingly competitive market environment."
According to comments from Metacore in May, its restructure and resulting acquisition by Supercell aims to "better align with the core business, improve efficiency of operations, and respond to an increasingly competitive market environment." This comes at a time where Merge Mansion 's growth has "plateaued over the past few years" since its 2020 launch, as well when new investments have not succeeded in launching new games globally.
Related: Gamecity Hamburg launches second round of prototype funding
Once the deal is closed, Merge Mansion will officially become part of Supercell's live games portfolio. In the meantime, both companies are already working to plan the transition of the game.
"As we move into this next phase together with Supercell, I'm excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team and our players," Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski says in this week's announcement . "Supercell's expertise in operating and growing global live games over many years gives Merge Mansion the best possible foundation for long-term success."
The Next Phase of Metacore
The acquisition is just one part of what Metacore called "its next phase" back in May. At the time, uncertainty over Merge Mansion's future led to the company initiating change negotiations in Finland. According to information shared at the time, the studio would "consider reducing up to 160 roles" in the country if plans were to be realized.
Moreover, Metacore was also investigating "what kind of changes there could be" to operations in Germany and Sweden. None of these plans are mentioned in this most recent deal announcement. In addition, the terms of the transaction will not be disclosed.
"These are very difficult discussions," Tammenkoski said in the announcement back in May. "We have built an organization with growth ambitions that have not materialized as expected. The competition has become tougher every year since we launched Merge Mansion and created the 'merge 2' category as a pioneer. We need to make changes to remain competitive and to give Merge Mansion the best possible chance to succeed going forward."
Related: CD Projekt Red won't be abandoning physical releases
Supercell, which sits under the Tencent umbrella, has spent the last couple of years buying majority stakes in and acquiring studios . In 2022, Supercell also ended development on two of its projects: Clash Quest and Everdale .
In April, the studio CEO and co-founder received a BAFTA Fellowship award in recognition of his long-standing contribution to the video game industry.

title: Xbox to cap Cloud Gaming hours for Game Pass subscribers
text:
Game Pass subscribers will no longer have unlimited access to Xbox's Cloud Gaming service.
Microsoft is rolling out new monthly limits on its Cloud Gaming service that will cap the number of hours that Game Pass subscribers can spend streaming games via cloud game technology. The restrictions—announced today via Xbox Wire —will levy stronger restrictions on users paying for cheaper versions of Xbox Game Pass.
Starting in November 2026, Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers will be able to stream games through Cloud Gaming for only 15 hours per month. Game Pass premium subscribers will be able to stream games for only 10 hours per month. And Game Pass Essential subscribers will only have 5 hours per month to use the service.
The company believes that this change will only "impact" 4 percent of Game Pass subscribers.
According to Microsoft, the company is introducing these change because "the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer."
"Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost."
Players who wish to continue using Xbox Cloud Gaming after hitting the monthly time limit will be able to do so if they purchase additional "playtime hours" through the Xbox Store.
Can Cloud Gaming "playtime hours" lure Xbox One owners into playing Xbox Series X|S games?
While Microsoft acknowledges that the new caps may create a "higher cost" for some players, it's also making something of an affordability pitch for existing Xbox One owners who still haven't purchased an Xbox Series X|S. The company is making these playtime hour purchases available to Xbox users who don't have a Game Pass subscription.
"This will provide another option for people who want occasional access to cloud gaming or do not want a recurring Game Pass subscription," the company explained. "Cloud gaming can also give XBOX One owners access to eligible games built for XBOX Series X|S without requiring an immediate hardware upgrade."
If this pitch sounds familiar, it's because reducing the price of Xbox services has been a major talking point for Xbox CEO Asha Sharma in interviews conducted in the wake of laying off 1,600 employees (with another 1,600 still at risk of being let go). She's explained that Microsoft needs to improve the affordability of its devices and services in the face of increasing hardware and memory costs. Said costs began to increase after the Trump administration imposed tariffs on foreign-produced goods and generative AI firms like OpenAI struck exclusive deals for to purchase years of memory chips used in console devices (Microsoft is a major financial partner of OpenAI).
There is one other target market for Xbox's new Cloud Gaming playtime hour purchase system: those who haven't been able to purchase an Xbox because the devices are "unavailable or unaffordable" in their region. If players can't afford an Xbox because currency rates elevate the device's price in their region, perhaps a few hours of playing Gears of War: E-Day will do.

title: Trump’s White House has made MAGA versions of Snake, Flappy Bird, Tetris and more
text:
The US government has developed five webgames that put a MAGA spin on several classic mobile and console games.
The new Arcade.gov portal on the US government’s website now hosts its own versions of Snake, Flappy Bird, Tetris and Duck Hunt, and promises more to come.
The MAGA spin on Flappy Bird is called Flappy Bill, and replaces the yellow bird and green pipes of the original with a bald eagle and White House-like columns.
Snake is reworked as Rio Run, and asks players to pick up and deport a growing line of people crossing the Rio Grande. There’s also a version of Tetris in which players build a wall to “protect the border from the coming horde”.
Trump Savings Tycoon is a Duck Hunt-like game where players tap or click the flying items to deposit them in their Trump account. Supply Line sees players tap unhealthy food items on a conveyor belt to remove them from a child’s school lunch.
The five games as they appear on arcade.gov.
There’s at least one more game coming soon to the new games portal – a sixth spot on the webpage says players should “stay tuned” and that “a new adventure awaits”.
The White House-made games were announced on X using videos that use old Xbox , PlayStation , Nintendo and Sega console start-up sequences.
The US government also posted a Pac-Man like image that reads ‘ Trump Arcade ’ with the message “Enter the arcade of winning”.

title: 触乐怪话：播客初体验
text:
触乐怪话，每天胡侃和游戏有关的屁事、鬼事、新鲜事。
原来这就是云里雾里！图/小罗
前段时间，我和朋友聊起：我想拥有一点活人感，还想增加一些生活趣味，有什么法子？他说，不如来录期播客吧。
我对这个提议有些惊喜，也有些犹豫。毕竟，从学生时代起，脱稿讲话必定是我的噩梦。和朋友闲聊可以，我愿意把故事讲得有趣一些，将那些曲折的部分描述得尽量离奇，甚至加上夸张的表情和动作。这样效果总不会太差。但是，要让人正襟危坐讲些什么，比如打辩论、上台讲正课PPT，我总觉得思维在天空飞，也不知道如何让它们变得有趣。
所以，其实我挺担心自己在播客里会无话可讲。
欸，是什么来着？
但我同时又有些兴奋。毕竟这可是我的播客初体验，还能写一篇夜话呢。
于是，我参加了这期播客，和朋友一起聊聊音游。怎么说呢，全程我的角色有些错位，我总想问问题，挑起话头。我最快乐的时候，是问问题，其次是用开玩笑的方式挑衅熟人。有冲突，就会有趣。但要让我说话，我会说些看起来非常深奥的话。总之就是一点都不好笑。
我发誓，我其实有提前准备。在开聊前，我围绕“从《节奏天国：奇迹之星》出发聊聊音游”这个话题准备了一些问题，也提前准备了一些回答。这个过程很有趣，能够帮助自己思考和整理思路，但坏就坏在我准备了不少延伸问题，关于《节奏天国：节奏之星》的回答，我还没来得及思考，播客就开始了。
我真的有准备哟
在开头，我在情绪激昂地介绍了自己的网名后，非常认真地说：“《节奏天国》是最有趣的音游。”朋友找到了机会：“你说是‘最有趣’。这是为什么呢？”这个问题我没准备过……于是我语气弱弱地说：“因为它很无厘头呀，你还能给洋葱拔胡子呢，太有趣了。”我感受到一种不太兴奋的氛围，这时有人帮我重复了一句：“对，很无厘头。”
我始终觉得这句话太过贫瘠，完全没有描述出《节奏天国》到底有多有趣。这可是一款可以给洋葱拔胡子的游戏呀。玩家还可以当青蛙伴舞，跳错了，就会看见一同伴舞的青蛙忧伤地看着你，而自己流着汗，显得非常窝囊，然后，我就会莫名其妙地觉得很好笑。笑够了，下一把再继续努力。
昨晚再体验，全程都在被青蛙盯着看
总之，我当时开了一个相当平凡的开头。后面开始问问题时，我倒有些自在。但是，又和我的朋友开始打架，因为这期播客主要由他主导节奏。
我中间开始思考播客这种形式，它似乎和采访有些相似，两人之间一问一答。但它其实更像那种对谈，双方有来有回地交流。当现场有三个人时，或许由一个人主导提问比较好。但三个人的回答汇聚在一起，又会碰撞出一些有趣的观点。
《节奏天国》的插图真的让人无语又好笑（别擦了，是拍的屏幕上有灰尘）
一小时很快过去，按下结束录制的键后，我松了一口气。我们反而聊起了更多平和有趣的内容。
对了，最后收尾的问题，我也回答得异常尴尬，有种高中生写论文强行升华的语调。（其实今天中午听了一遍，没有我想得那么坏。）
总之，这是一次有趣的经历。但你要想让我指路，那我只能说这是秘密。因为现在回想起来，心里的感受就是，好好笑。算了，下一把再努力。（以及没有吃到凉拌菠萝，但吃到了烤菠萝）

title: 在电影和电视剧里讲游戏故事，这家公司是专业的
text:
“这项工作确实变得比以前更容易了，却也不像一些人想象中那么容易。”影视制片公司Story Kitchen联合创始人德米特里·约翰逊（Dmitri Johnson）说。按照约翰逊和另一位联合创始人迈克·戈德堡（Mike Goldberg）的说法，虽然近年来有一大批改编自热门游戏的影视剧在票房和口碑层面获得成功，但当他俩试图向其他制片厂的高层推销基于游戏IP的影视项目时，整个过程仍然充满挑战。
Story Kitchen是参与制作《古墓丽影》《刺猬索尼克》和《光与影：33号远征队》等游戏改编影视剧的工作室之一
“我们每天都在努力改变人们对游戏的刻板印象：很多人始终认为，电子游戏只适合小孩子，以及那些无所事事，成天窝在家里的宅男。”约翰逊苦笑着补充，“但事实上，游戏开发者也是艺术家和讲述故事的人，他们的作品值得被更多人看到。”
■ 开始游戏
你很可能不太了解Story Kitchen，但肯定听说过这家公司曾参与制作的游戏改编影视作品，例如派拉蒙影业发行的“刺猬索尼克”系列电影、Netflix的“古墓丽影”动画剧，以及将在亚马逊流媒体平台Prime Video播出的《奇异人生》《古墓丽影》真人剧集。某种意义而言，Story Kitchen正站在游戏衍生影视作品“黄金时代”的最前沿。
上世纪90年代到本世纪初，大量游戏改编电影因质量糟糕饱受诟病，包括《超级马力欧兄弟》（1993年上映）、《毁灭战士》（2005年）和《死亡之屋》（2003年）等，其中，《死亡之屋》更沦为了知名影评网站烂番茄历史评分最低的影片之一。戈德堡指出，那些古早游戏改编电影之所以纷纷遭遇失败，很大程度上是因为众多娱乐巨头未能充分理解原作。“如今回头来看，这确实有点像电子游戏改编作品遭到的一种诅咒。”戈德堡说，“在那个年代，好莱坞制片公司普遍对游戏玩家、开发商和发行商缺乏尊重，电子游戏似乎注定会被边缘化，永远无法走到视觉媒体领域的舞台中央。”
2011年，德米特里·约翰逊和丹·杰文斯（Dan Jevons）联合创办dj2娱乐公司（Story Kitchen的前身——译注），迈出了探索未知领域的第一步。Dj2的主要目标很简单，那就是向好莱坞公司展示游戏故事的潜力，并说服他们投入资金，打造基于游戏IP的影视作品。然而，由于好莱坞大厂并不看好这门生意的前景，Dj2曾经屡屡碰壁，遭到了无数次拒绝。
2020年，动作科幻喜剧电影《刺猬索尼克》获得了巨大成功
首部《刺猬索尼克》真人电影成了Dj2发展历程中的转折点。经过长期沟通，约翰逊一步步赢得了日本游戏发行商世嘉的信任和尊重，使世嘉和派拉蒙影业公司相信，人们渴望看到蓝色刺猬索尼克在一部属于自己的电影中亮相。《刺猬索尼克》在制作期间遭遇了一些挫折，比如当首支预告片发布后，索尼克的形象引起众多玩家抨击，制作团队不得不迅速重新设计……不过2020年初，尽管疫情导致《刺猬索尼克》的院线放映提前结束，这部电影仍然斩获3.2亿美元的全球票房，票房收入远远超过了制作和营销成本（约9000万美元）。
“约翰逊始终相信，只要制片公司真正理解并尊重游戏IP，就能够打造出成功的游戏改编作品。”戈德堡指出，“事实证明他是对的。”
■ 精挑细选
自从《刺猬索尼克》上映以来，游戏改编热潮的兴起促使影视行业发生了翻天覆地的变化，戈德堡将这些变化描述为“好莱坞生态系统的一次彻底变革”。过去几年间，改编自《超级马力欧兄弟》《我的世界》等热门游戏IP的电影在全球拿下数十亿美元票房，《最后生还者》《辐射》电视剧和游戏衍生动画剧集《英雄联盟：双城之战》等作品也广受好评，斩获多项大奖，并向数百万观众呈现了他们以前从未接触过的故事、角色和世界。
随着游戏改编作品迎来爆发式增长，dj2一直在积累经验，提升自身实力。2022年10月，dj2宣布品牌升级，将团队和项目转移到新成立的影视制作公司Story Kitchen。从那以后，Story Kitchen招募了伊莲娜·桑多瓦尔（Elena Sandoval）、蒂莫西·I·史蒂文森（Timothy I. Stevenson）和达拉斯·狄金森（Dalls Dickinson）等业内资深人士担任高管，还先后在2022年2月和2024年5月，与亚马逊和梦工厂动画公司签署了优先合作协议。
《我的世界大电影》画面
Story Kitchen致力于打造以游戏IP为根基的爆款跨媒介作品。在现阶段，Story Kitchen总部手握大约30个项目，并已经为部分项目找到买家，正在四处推销其他项目。这个数字听起来似乎很夸张，在电子游戏的汪洋里却犹如沧海一粟……那么，Story Kitchen为什么不直接带着一份写满游戏名称的清单去拜访电影制片厂、电视台和流媒体平台，以这种遍地撒网的方式谈合作呢？毕竟，从理论上讲，总有一款游戏能引起影视公司的兴趣。
“我们正处于一个新时代，但并非所有游戏都适合被改编。”戈德堡指出，“无论如何，Story Kitchen渴望长期深耕这一领域，因为我们坚信，游戏改编的热潮绝非昙花一现，而是拥有长远潜力。”
除了3A大作之外，Story Kitchen还长期对2A游戏和独立游戏保持关注。“当我们向潜在合作方推荐IP时，根本不想谈论‘这款游戏卖了多少份？’之类的问题。”约翰逊透露，“事实上，我们鄙视那个问题，往往拒绝回答。在与潜在合作方的沟通中，我们更倾向于解释为什么游戏里的故事和角色精彩绝伦，或者它具备哪些人们从未见过的亮点。”
“归根结底，我们只会挑选能够让我们产生浓厚兴趣，并倾注热情的游戏。一旦我们心里有了目标，觉得必须将某个游戏IP改编成影视作品，就会向其他公司卖力推荐……起初，对方未必理解我们的想法，但仍然想听听我们的方案，因为我们表现出了强烈的热情。当我们带着项目提案上门拜访时，大多数电视台和制片厂的高层都很乐意与我们聊聊。他们非常清楚，我们并非为了捞钱与他们谈合作，而是真心希望打造出高质量的游戏改编作品。”
■ 蓄势待发
《古墓丽影》真人剧剧照
约翰逊和戈德堡总是认真对待Story Kitchen参与制作的每一部游戏改编作品。截至目前，“刺猬索尼克”系列已经推出三部高票房电影和衍生真人剧集《纳克鲁斯》（Knuckles），《刺猬索尼克4》则已进入后期制作阶段，将于2027年3月19日在北美上映。另外，一部据传以暗影（Shadow）为主角、暂未定名的衍生电影也在制作中，但约翰逊和戈德堡拒绝透露细节。“我们必须遵守保密协议。”戈德堡说。
2027年，Story Kitchen参与制作的两部电视剧将会在亚马逊流媒体平台Prime Video播出，其中之一是经典动作冒险游戏《古墓丽影》的真人剧集。菲比·沃勒-布里奇担任该剧的编剧兼执行制作人，苏菲·特纳将饰演主角劳拉·克劳馥。
按照约翰逊的说法，在Netflix动画剧集《古墓丽影》制作期间，Story Kitchen与游戏工作室水晶动力（Crystal Dynamics）建立了良好的合作关系。“作为合作伙伴，我们希望在未来再次携手，并为此制定了非常清晰的计划。”因此，当亚马逊提议为《古墓丽影》制作真人剧集时，Story Kitchen和水晶动力似乎迎来了一次千载难逢的机会。
“剧组的每个决定都需要经过水晶动力批准。”约翰逊透露，“《古墓丽影》第一季得到了水晶动力的认可，他们积极参与其中，同时非常尊重《古墓丽影》铁杆玩家菲比的想法……事实上，前段时间我们已经开始观看《古墓丽影》真人剧的初剪版，全程都像10岁小孩那样笑个不停。我对这部剧的质量很有信心。”
“顺便提一句，我们不是那种喜欢自吹自擂的人。如果你妈妈观看《古墓丽影》真人剧，她不会觉得这部剧改编自一个拥有30年历史的电子游戏系列。我们不想将《古墓丽影》改编成一部只面向核心玩家的粉丝向作品。当然，我们尊重玩家，会努力让玩家感受到被重视，但我们的目标是让那些从未玩过《古墓丽影》游戏的新观众，也像我们一样爱上这部剧。”
《奇异人生》游戏截图
《奇异人生》是另一部将于2027年登陆Prime Video平台的新剧，作为联合制片方，Story Kitchen遇到了与制作《古墓丽影》完全不同的挑战。《奇异人生》真人剧改编自2015年问世的同名冒险游戏，后者采用章节体结构，讲述了一位拥有“时间倒流”能力的高中生麦克斯的故事。游戏原作以基于对话选项的分支叙事闻名，不过，玩家所做的选择最终只会导向两个结局中的一个。在项目筹备和剧本创作阶段，Story Kitchen怎样改编原作中基于玩家选择、不断演变的故事？他们又如何决定采用哪个结局？毕竟，“奇异人生”系列未来还会推出新作，讲述麦克斯的全新故事，而一些观众可能将电视剧结局当成真正的官方结局。
“在《奇异人生》游戏中，几乎所有重大决定都令玩家左右为难，选择不同选项的玩家可能各占一半。”约翰逊指出，“我们从一开始就很清楚，任何结局都不可能令所有人满意。话虽如此，我认为许多观众会为我们对游戏里某些关键决策的处理方式感到高兴，甚至很可能被电视剧的结局所感动。”
与此同时，Story Kitchen和亚马逊米高梅影业正在全力推进瑞典工作室Hazelight旗下两款高口碑游戏的电影改编项目，分别是《双人成行》和《双影奇境》。其中，《双影奇境》真人电影仍处于早期开发阶段，不过戈德堡证实，知名演员西德妮·斯威尼、“魔法坏女巫”系列电影的导演朱浩伟、《死侍》编剧雷特·里斯和保罗·韦尼克参与了该项目。
“你可以和伴侣、朋友或家人一起玩游戏，每个人能从中获得自己的体验。”戈德堡说，“我们如何诠释这些体验，并将它们转变成观众共同的感受？这本身就是一项充满乐趣的挑战。作为电影编剧，里斯和韦尼克甚至坚持亲自玩一玩《双影奇境》，而这肯定会对他们创作的剧本产生影响。”
双人合作冒险游戏《双影奇境》将被改编成一部真人电影
与《双影奇境》真人电影相比，Hazelight工作室另一款游戏《双人成行》改编电影的制作进度缓慢得多。早在2022年，巨石强森的Seven Bucks制片公司就宣布加入这个由亚马逊主导的项目，然而，Hazelight创意总监约瑟夫·法尔斯在去年2月接受媒体采访时透露，他对《双人成行》电影改编项目的状况几乎一无所知。
“好莱坞的繁琐流程太多，有些事情看似板上钉钉，其实八字都没一撇。”法尔斯直言，“我觉得在好莱坞，90%的会议都是扯淡……很多时候，参与谈判的各方光说不练，没有把计划落到实处。我不知道到底发生了什么，但愿能看到成果吧。如果《双人成行》电影能够与观众们见面，那当然很好，不过我不抱太大希望。”
当被问到法尔斯、Hazelight和巨石强森是否仍然参与《双人成行》影视剧项目时，约翰逊表示：“是的。如今我们与Hazelight团队关系密切，彼此间形成了一种默契。我们和Hazelight以及其他合作伙伴的沟通都非常顺畅。”
■ 枝繁叶茂
《师父》真人电影将在Netflix平台播出
这只是Story Kitchen计划推进的30多个影视项目中的冰山一角。按照约翰逊和戈德堡的说法，Story Kitchen希望覆盖尽可能多的游戏类型和受众群体。目前，这家公司正在筹备3款Roblox游戏《种植花园》《Steal a Brainrot》和《Jailbreak》的电影改编项目，并与环球影业合作，为《正当防卫》《忍》和《Ruiner》制作真人电影。除此之外，Story Kitchen参与制片的其他游戏改编影视作品还包括《师父》《Kingsmaker》《怒之铁拳》《渔帆暗涌》和《死亡之屋》真人电影等。
Story Kitchen的业务并不局限于将游戏改编为电影。过去两年间，Story Kitchen还在制作一部《玩具反斗城》真人电影，以及一部以会说话的玩具熊特迪·华斯比（Teddy Puxpin）为主角的电影。“我觉得它跟《芭比》（2023年上映）有点像。”约翰逊说，“我一开始的想法是‘哎，又有人想圈钱了’，但当看到第三幕时，我竟然有点想哭……这部电影的搞笑程度可能超出人们的想象。我们加入了一些看似荒诞的歌舞元素，并以一种绝妙的方式将它们与剧情完美融合。总之，我相信它会让观众感到惊喜，孩子们看完电影后肯定想要一只特迪·华斯比玩具熊。”
Story Kitchen希望特迪·华斯比电影能够像2023年上映的《芭比》那样火爆
就游戏改编项目而言，Story Kitchen 不仅仅将经典旧作和当下热门游戏视为潜在的改编对象，还会关注一些仍处于开发阶段的新游戏。“我们正在为一款尚未公布的游戏筹备剧集，并即将向潜在合作方介绍相关方案。”戈德堡透露，“如果一切顺利，开发商将会在2026年TGA颁奖典礼期间正式公布这款游戏。不过，我们下个月就会带着一份制作精美，包含完整剧本的电视剧提案拜访各大制片厂，以便在游戏官宣后迅速推进项目。”
约翰森补充，早在《光与影：33号远征队》发售前，Story Kitchen就与这款回合制角色扮演游戏的法国研发工作室Sandafall达成了合作。“Story Kitchen从不追逐热度，我们为此感到自豪。”约翰逊说，“一旦某款游戏成为热门大作，我们追求它的动力就会下降，因为我们不想被人们视为一家盲目跟风的公司。”
“事实上，我们从2023年就开始与Sandfall合作了。我们阅读了近600页剧本，听原始的音乐文件，还欣赏了大量美术设计，在看到游戏的任何实机画面前就深深爱上了它……当然，谁都无法预知一款游戏的销量，所以我们早就知道，如果《光与影：33号远征队》卖得不好，我们将很难向其他制片公司推销我们制定的电影改编计划。但正如我之前所说，一旦我们对某个项目燃起热情，就不会轻易接受‘不’。我们始终相信，这是一个值得我们投入的项目。”
Story Kitchen正在与Sandfall联手制作《光与影：33号远征队》真人电影
尽管Story Kitchen已经手握30多个项目，约翰逊和戈德堡仍然渴望将更多经典IP改编成影视作品。约翰逊透露，他梦想着将“洛克人”和“龙行忍者”（Bad Dudes）搬上大荧幕，戈德堡最念念不忘的IP则是任天堂的经典科幻游戏系列“密特罗德”（Metroid）。
某种意义而言，在约翰逊和戈德堡的领导下，Story Kitchen正在重塑跨媒体娱乐领域。
“前不久，我们回顾了去年英国电影与电视艺术学院游戏奖（BAFTA Game Awards）的候选游戏名单，其中包含由一支澳大利亚小团队开发的点击冒险游戏《漂泊者》（The Dirfter）。”约翰逊回忆，“作为BAFTA的评委，自从2025年偶然发现《漂泊者》以来，我一直对它赞不绝口。经过一番努力，我们与《漂泊者》的开发团队建立联系，并在与另一家制片公司的首次谈判中就达成合作意向，对方同意将这款游戏改编成一部真人电影。”
“如果时间回到五六年前，这一切根本不可能发生。如今，Story Kitchen已经走完第一步，打破了‘游戏改编作品被诅咒’这种愚蠢观念。接下来我们将会迈出第二步，那就是郑重其事地告诉大家，游戏改编的影视作品有能力赢得奥斯卡、艾美奖和英国电影学院奖等权威奖项。这是我们的下一个目标：证明电子游戏也是艺术。我们将会努力让人们看到，电子游戏讲述的故事、塑造的角色……都与在《纽约时报》榜单中排名前列的畅销书并无二致。”
本文编译自： techradar
原文标题：《'That's our next mission — proving that games are art': meet Story Kitchen, the bold, trail-blazing studio behind the popular Sonic movies that wants to turn your favorite game into the next movie or TV hit》
原作者：Tom Power

title: 《致命躯壳2》：魂Like红海的另类解？
text:
《致命躯壳2》：魂Like红海的另类解？
原创 作者：西北偏北 23小时前 5.3k
谁曾想， 2026 年暑假档的最后一周，又有一匹黑马吸引了无数人的眼球：
就在这个盛产雷霆雨露的闷热时节，一部圈外少有人看好的无名续作，横空出世将名号响亮的《轮回之兽》掀翻在地，一举拿下了 Steam 销量榜冠军，成为了彼时 “ 魂 Like” 游戏赛道最闪耀的新星 —— 这，就是《致命躯壳 2 》。
乍看之下，这似乎又是个 “ 值得吹嘘一下的翻身范本 ”—— 但是且慢，和大多数 “ 初代平淡无奇，续作一鸣惊人 ” 的纯血黑马杰作不同，尽管拥有可观的社区讨论热度，但从实际反馈来看，《致命躯壳 2 》基本只能落在 “ 多半好评 ” 的区间当中 —— 倘若再筛选一下语种，简中环境下的 “ 褒贬不一 ” 更是让人印象深刻 —— 那么，这部热度与质疑同样可观的作品，究竟是欺世盗名的骗局，还是过于另类导致争议不断的杰作？在这部作品身上，究竟有没有值得我们借鉴学习的亮点？
没错，这次的经验之谈，就让我们聊点不一样的东西吧 ——
“可怕的游戏”
《致命躯壳 2 》，究竟是怎么个成色的游戏？
放在以往，想要描述这种作品，免不了要长篇大论半天 —— 不过，拜时效有限但胜在鲜明易懂的网络热梗所赐，如今想要定义《致命躯壳 2 》，一个词足矣：
这是一部货真价实的 “ 雷霆 ” 游戏。
至于说雷点在哪 —— 首先，打开游戏截图看一眼，我相信至少九成左右的朋友都要被这玩意的画风直接劝退：
迥异于正统 “ 魂 ” 系列破败但不失威严的古典 / 新古典艺术风格，《致命躯壳 2 》的画风就像是 H·G·Giger 的奇妙趣味，混合了 Zdzis ł aw Beksi ń ski 的 “ 有机 ” 质感；换句话来说，对于极端金属音乐（尤其是 20 世纪 90 年代到千禧年前后那一波）有爱的朋友们，多半也会对这种画风爱得深沉 —— 可惜这类型在国内听众圈子里属于不折不扣的小众，因此第一印象大骂 “ 这都是一坨什么鬼 ” 的国内玩家属实不在少数，风评不佳的直接理由，便是如此。
其次，即便熬过了画风这一关，实际上手一试便知， 《致命躯壳 2 》诚如其名，把 “ 致命 ” 体现得淋漓尽致：
如果诸位是从《艾尔登法环》入坑 “ 魂 ” 系列的朋友，那这个机动性、灵活性直降一个档次的主角绝对得适应一下（更不用说那个全是槽点的镜头调校）；并且，即便是从 “ 魂 ” 系列上道的老玩家，面对崭新的敌人也得小心行事 —— 虽然没有体力条限制似乎挺好，但在游戏开始的前半小时之内，我们面对的是动辄一个连段就能砍掉我们 70%HP 、且次次组队出没的狂野杂兵（们），且在途中还会遇到一个擅长召唤自爆小怪、被炸一回基本出局、出局又要从头跑一路的道中 Boss—— 正所谓从奢入简难，经历过《艾尔登法环》这种完善太多的新作品还要回头重新吃苦，实话实说，不太快乐。
然而，假如真的头铁一下熬过这一关，《致命躯壳 2 》呈现给我们的正式面貌，完全就是另一副模样 ——
进入《致命躯壳 2 》的核心枢纽（大致等同于传火祭祀场）之后，稍加探索，我们很容易就能从一处台座上，找到一件名叫 “ 屠杀者印记 ” 的奇妙装备：
在正式装备之前，游戏会反复提醒我们 “ 一旦装备就无法在当前游戏解锁成就 ”—— 不过即便如此，如果诸位是第一次体验《致命躯壳 2 》且受了一肚子气寻思着要不要退款走人的话，那我强烈建议，诸位试过这件装备之后再下决定也不迟：
简单来说，这件装备的功效，就是允许我们使用一种蓄力发动的特殊攻击 —— 一旦命中敌人，不仅可以造成海量伤害，更能几乎瞬间为我们补满多半截损失的血条，同时还能恢复大部分发动其他特殊攻击的资源条，并将敌人打到几乎崩溃的临界状态 —— 这还是对上 Boss 以及精英怪的场合，通常的路边小怪，挨上这么一下基本就是立刻扑街的命；
虽然基本只能单发攻击是个缺陷，但架不住资源回复率实在太高，再加上射程距离（没错，虽然这是一招近战，但可以远远跑到敌人巡视范围边缘直接蓄力，然后呼啸而去一拳把怪打翻）长得惊人， 一旦装上了 “ 屠杀者印记 ” ，紧随而至的就是荡气回肠的长出一口恶气 —— 这种吃苦积攒的怨仇当场结清的爽感，正是《致命躯壳 2 》大部分游戏流程当中，最核心的乐趣所在。
事实上，只要是 撑过最开始最难熬的序章 ，进入正篇之后，《致命躯壳 2 》五花八门的构筑配方，各种多多少少带点崩坏却又能打得堆质又堆量的敌人（们）抱头鼠窜的奇妙 build ，这种核心主旨在于 “ 图一爽 ” 的特性，就成为了《致命躯壳 2 》令人大悦的关键游戏乐趣所在；
虽然目前版本的大后期确实还有点问题（主要是数值架构做得确实有点离谱），外加程序水平一般导致不少莫名其妙的 bug 直接改变了游戏的构筑玩法，但即便是以现如今的版本来看，粗糙有余的《致命躯壳 2 》，确实也走出了一条迥异于 “ 自讨苦吃 ” 刻板印象的另类 “ 魂 ”Like 游戏新路径 —— 即便需要完善的细节、重新修正的程序错漏还有不少，但《致命躯壳 2 》整体的系统架构，已经足以证明 “ 魂 Like” 这个类型的潜力，远不止 “ 受苦 ” 这种刻板印象那么单纯。
那么，从专业从业者的角度来看，《致命躯壳 2 》究竟是一帮怎样的开发者攒出来的作品？藉此找到灵感的我们，又应当如何规划设计，才能拿出青出于蓝、引人入胜更甚一筹的新企划？
别急，让给我们一步一步来看 ——
当一群资深美工开始组队……
在游戏行业打拼多年，厌倦了扮演 3A 流水线上的螺丝钉，决定出门单干 —— 这是许多我们耳熟能详的 “ 行业老兵离职创业做独立游戏 ” 故事的开头 —— 《致命躯壳》系列背后的开发商 Cold Symmetry 也不例外；不过，和那些 “ 所有职位人手齐备再行动 ” 的 “ 布莱梅乐队 ” 故事不同， Cold Symmetry 的创始团队，可以说从一开始就把 “ 偏科 ” 写在了脸上：
Vitaly Bulgarov （联合创始人 / 艺术创意总监）
暴雪出身的资深设计师，参与项目包括《星际争霸 2 》《暗黑破坏神 3 》以及《魔兽世界》等经典，常年负责 CG 与概念艺术创作；离职暴雪后曾入职工业光魔等知名视效公司，参与《攻壳机动队》（真人版）、《阿丽塔：战斗天使》《变形金刚 4 》以及《终结者：创世纪》的机械设定工作，除此之外，著名载人双足机甲 “METHOD-​2” 的工业外观设计也是由他负责 —— 换言之不管是数字艺术还是实体工程设计，这位前暴雪老兵都是拿得起玩得转。
Dmitry Parkin （联合创始人 / 创意与怪物设计艺术家）
业内知名 3D 数字怪物创作者，在过去超过 20 年的时间中，曾参与项目包括《辐射 3 》《地铁：最后的曙光》《教团： 1886 》以及《光环：士官长合集》知名 3A 大作系列，主要负责角色与怪兽模型制作；成立 Cold Symmetry 工作室之前，曾经在 Sucker Punch 认知资深角色设计师， TGA 2020  最佳艺术指导奖得主《对马岛之魂》，即出自这位的手笔。
Anton Gonzalez （联合创始人 / 联合总监 & 环境 & 技术美术专家）
尽管知名度较之前两位略逊一筹，但这位 Cold Symmetry 初始团队成员，同样在 Sucker Punch 以及动视有过任职，包括《对马岛之魂》在内的项目皆有参与；并且，和前两位队友相比，这位的核心工作还包括将美术资源与底层代码的对接 —— 换句话来说，从系列标志性的 “ 硬化 ” ，再到从 DEMO 阶段就开始冒头的各种莫名其妙的 “ 场景构件失踪 ”bug ，基本都是这位的功绩（？）。
Andrew McLennan-​Murray （联合创始人 / 总监 / 系统程序）
没错，这就是团队的技术架构 / 游戏玩法负责人了，《致命躯壳》这个系列的原型，最开始就是这位和上面的 Anton Gonzalez 联手在虚幻引擎中摸索出来的， “ 硬化 ” 机制的逻辑更是离不开他的建设，同时，《致命躯壳 2 》从整体方向到架构执行，同样都是交由这位负责；发行后的改进完善以及修 Bug ，也离不开这位的工作 —— 换言之，他应该就是 Cold Symmetry 当下最忙的那一位。
综上所述，我们不难看出，整个 Cold Symmetry 团队的创始核心成员，美工出身起码占了大半 —— 正因如此，我们才会在《致命躯壳 2 》当中欣赏到另类十足却又不乏美感的视觉设计；同时，对于自身团队的短板， Cold Symmetry 上下同样十分清楚，在 “ 充分利用 UE 引擎机能降低工作量优化性能 ” 的同时，玩法设计层面的 “ 扬长避短 ” 主旨，从一开始就被提上了议程：
首先，在《致命躯壳》初代当中，确实包含一些初见印象足够另类、滋味俨然 “ 独此一家 ” 的设计，但从实际的市场反响来看，似乎并不足以支撑起整部作品在市场上瓜分 “ 魂 Like” 游戏的基本盘；
正因如此，在《致命躯壳 2 》当中， Cold Symmetry 直接拿掉了传统 “ 魂 Like” 游戏似乎必不可少的 “ 体力槽 ” ，转而用 “ 必须进攻才能积攒 ” 的特殊攻击资源条构筑起了整套系统 —— 如果诸位对于一线 ACT ，以及包括《毁灭战士》在内的现代爽游 FPS 不陌生的话，应该一眼就能看出这套系统的原型；同时，这也就是前文提到的 “ 屠杀者印记 ” 强得离谱的核心理由：
命中即可大幅回血还是其次，整套攻击系统的资源管理学习曲线被这个近乎作弊的可怕道具一拳干挺，换言之就像是在《毁灭战士》当中拿到了无限启动的电锯 —— 好吧，强得无趣确实是个问题，但看在确实很爽的份上，原谅一下似乎也不是不可以。
当然，这个强大到离谱且完全没有入手难度的装备，也确实给《致命躯壳 2 》引来了不少麻烦：
按照 Cold Symmetry 的想法，最初的预想中，这个完全改变了整套游戏系统基本平衡的道具，其实压根就不是什么 “ 官方作弊器 ” ，而是另一套 “ 魂式爽游 ” 模式的启动开关，甚至还包含完整的成就模式 —— 然而遗憾的是，受限于主机平台的合规认证，以及实体光盘提前数月压盘进厂的硬性规程，成就系统的底层配置一旦定型，便无法像数字版在线热更新那样随时回炉；等到 Cold Symmetry 想要实现预想的 “ 双线成就 ” 系统时，方才发现为时已晚 —— 因此，面对社区玩家的抱怨，除了 “ 会作为免费 DLC 进行考虑 ” 之外，目前版本的《致命躯壳 2 》，确实只能体验这种爽归爽但确实不够尽兴的 “ 魂式爽游 ” 模式了。
但无论如何，从产品的角度出发，完成度有限的《致命躯壳 2 》，确实在系统设计方面做出了大胆的尝试 —— 我们接下来要做的，就是继续开拓一下思路， 在保留爽快感的同时，设计出功能维度不再单一的 “ 屠杀者印记 ” ，让不同的玩家各取所需，通过 “ 打光 HP 就能赢 ” 之外的手段体验到真正的多样化系统设计 —— 那么，能够实现这种维度的设计原型，在现如今的游戏市场上，真的存在吗？
答案当然是肯定的。
“技术击倒”的另一种可能
在现实世界的搏击竞技场当中， “ 如何击败敌人 ” ，最常见的有两种模式：
其一是直接通过不犯规的格斗手段，将对手直接打倒在擂台上；倘若经过一段时间对手依旧无力起身，那就可以判定己方获胜 —— 这就是 “ 击倒 ” ，也就是格斗游戏里最常见的 “K.O.” 。
其二，即便并未将对手打倒在地，但如果场上的裁判和医生判定其人无法继续比赛，或者对手的教练乃至对手本身决定弃赛，那么即便未能满足 “ 击倒 ” 的客观条件，也可以判定己方获胜 —— 这就是 “ 技术击倒 ” ，即 “T.K.O.” 。
由此可见，从观赏体验的角度来看，不拘泥于 “ 扣光血条 ” 这一种胜利方式，对于规模更甚游戏玩家不止一筹的主流观众而言，本身并不是什么不可接受的主题；而在另一方面，对于发展积累远超现如今主流游戏（没错， “ 魂 ” 系列在它们面前同样是小字辈）的经典游戏类型来说，迥异于 “HP 清零 ” 且同样能够 “ 击倒敌人 ” 的战斗胜利方案，早已不是什么新鲜事：
让我们再来看看 《龙与地下城》。
作为 “ 角色职业（ Classes ） ”“ 经验等级（ Levels/​XP ） ”“ 护甲等级（ AC ） ” 乃至 “ 生命值（ HP ） ” 等等一系列专业名词的经典 TRPG 规则， “ 战胜对手 ” 的方式，堪称是 “ 多样性 ” 的典范：
打光 HP—— 这个我们都能理解，和主流游戏一样；除此之外，通过特定手段 “ 削减属性 ” ，也就是我们熟悉的力量、敏捷乃至智力这些攸关 “ 血条以外角色性能 ” 的面板数值，一旦清零，同样是瘫倒在地任人摆布的结局 —— 比 “ 打光 HP” 更关键的一点在于，这类削减通常不是一个两个血瓶就能扶起来的；再比如，利用某些特定的法术，同样可以实现 “ 等同于击败 ” 的效果 —— 例如 “ 无法通过常规手段唤醒的睡眠 ” ，这种原型一目了然的技术，在《龙与地下城》的游戏桌面上是完全可以成立的，尽管需求等级较高（可以理解）确实是个问题，不过一旦成功就能基本宣告全面胜利，考虑到这种 “ 不伤分毫的一发逆转 ” 性价比极高，乐于尝试的玩家自然是大有人在。
不仅如此，对于完全 “ 不想动手 ” 的玩家来说，这种经典游戏规则，同样为我们提供了大量 “ 不战而屈人之兵 ” 的好选择：化妆易容潜入挑拨离间仅仅是基础中的基础，制造幻象利用幻术迷惑敌人也不过是入门级的操作，直接控制心灵支配敌人去帮我们干活同样是 “ 标准 ” 程度的战术，至于直接 “ 支配 ” 敌人、占用强壮但缺乏智慧的对手躯体执行 “ 李代桃僵 ” 的操作，更是从上个世纪开始就有记载的经典玩法之一 —— 换言之，即便是 “ 魂 Like” 玩家，即便我们追求的不是 “ 依靠三寸不烂之舌不开一枪打穿游戏 ” 的经典 CRPG 套路，即便让我们把目光聚集在 “ 不是你死就是我活 ” 的 “ 战斗 ” 主题之上，来自 “ 龙与地下城 ” 这种 TRPG 的经验，依旧是不胜枚举。
正所谓 “ 攻其无备，出其不意 ”—— 不仅现实中的 “ 兵者，诡道也 ” 如此，游戏领域的《致命躯壳 2 》同样告诉我们，跳脱传统 “ 魂 Like” 游戏框架的 “ 多样化构筑 ” ，亦有其魅力蕴藏其中，我们真正要做的，仅仅是在这个思路的基础之上继续延伸拓展一下而已。
不仅仅是“魂游”
值得一提的是，《致命躯壳 2 》的经验、教训乃至相关尝试为我们呈现的效果，其实，并不一定局限在 “ 魂 Like” 这个范畴之内：
对于现如今受众更广、触达范围更大的主流类型（典型如二游），随着运营时间的不断延长，不断膨胀的数值导致越来越多的角色（其中不乏曾经的 MVP ）成为了仓库和冷板凳的常客，这种令所有人难堪的局面，早已成为了 “ 房间中的大象 ” 性质的显学 —— 因此，相较于单纯易懂但潜力有限的 “ 数值比大小 ” ，或许，适当运用一下 “ 四两拨千斤 ” 、通过其他维度撬动数值系统的策略，也是未尝不可。
虽然完全谈不上完美，但《致命躯壳 2 》确实为我们在 “ 魂 Like” 这个已然定型的子类型外壳上敲开了一条缝隙 —— 既然市场和玩家已经证明了这条 “ 不寻常的道路 ” 颇为受用，举一反三跳出名为 “ 产品规则 ” 实为 “ 刻板印象 ” 的窠臼，尝试一点新的配方，未必也不是另一种选择。（文/西北偏北）

title: One Of The Coziest Games Of The Year Is Helping Crunchyroll Game Vault Grow Even Bigger
text:
The Crunchyroll Game Vault is expanding, as the anime brand has announced several new additions to its collection of mobile games. Available as a membership perk for Mega and Ultimate Fan subscribers, the Game Vault will now offer more than 100 games free of ads and in-app purchases, with new arrivals like Baki Hanma: Blood Arena and ReStory: Chill Electronics Repairs being added to the service.
For fans of cozy experiences, ReStory is a delightful game where you run an electronics workshop and spend the day restoring old tech to working order while listening to some chill lofi beats. Designed to be satisfying and relaxing, it's a nostalgic look back at retro gaming hardware, cellphones, and other essential gadgets. Other upcoming games being added to Crunchyroll's vault include the stylish psychological-horror adventure Little Goody Two Shoes, the elegantly designed adventure Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley, and Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon, which reimagines the spade-wielding hero's quest as a roguelike with puzzle elements. Rounding out the arrivals is Streets of Rage 4 , which is still one of the best beat-'em-ups ever made.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XiYNNGR4uLo
Crunchyroll also added a few more games recently, like the 2D brawler Baki Hanma: Blood Arena, a monster-hunting adventure where you cook what you catch in Battle Chef Brigade, and Beyblade X Xone for fans of the blade-spinning anime and toy franchise.
If you're unfamiliar with it, the Crunchyroll Game Vault offers a curated library of premium mobile, indie, and anime-inspired games on iOS and Android devices. Available at no extra charge to Mega and Ultimate Fan members, this means that you're getting dozens of games on top of access to all the anime series and films through the streaming platform. Many titles also support Bluetooth gamepads (Xbox, PlayStation, or mobile controllers like the Backbone One) on mobile devices, so you're getting a traditional gaming experience if you have this hardware.
You can find this section in the Crunchyroll App, and it already includes several great games, such as Dungeons of Hinterberg, Pepper Grinder, and Metal Slug Tactics. If you're interested, the full list of games is below.
Considering how video game hardware is more expensive than ever before, Crunchyroll's Game Vault is a pretty solid deal considering how most people have access to smart devices. GameSpot recently took a look at how you can save some cash during Cheap Week , and if you missed it, you can check out our features on the best games for under $10 , game subscriptions you might already have , and why the future is friendslop .
